title: Single-cell multi-omic profiling allows the dissection of peripheral immune phenotypes in Alzheimer’s Disease progression

evidence_spans.quote: Here, we employed three high-resolution single-cell techniques
peripheral immunity in AD dementia
AD progression in contrast to healthy aging across cohorts
single-cell RNA- and ATAC-sequencing

scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This preprint reports completed patient-level biological analyses, explicitly contrasts findings with healthy aging, and analyzes transcriptomic plus epigenetic modalities.

causal_design_reviewer.exposure_or_intervention: Alzheimer’s disease dementia and earlier stages of the AD trajectory
causal_design_reviewer.outcome: Peripheral immune phenotypes, including B-cell compartment and classical monocyte inflammatory phenotype

evidence_spans.quote: Single-cell multi-omic profiling
We identified reduced humoral immune responses in AD
AD dementia and earlier stages of the AD trajectory
diminished B cell compartment
Classical monocytes expanded in mild cognitive impairment and early AD dementia
distinct phenotypes that define AD progression in contrast to healthy aging across cohorts

causal_design_reviewer.concise_rationale: The report presents cross-sectional multi-omic profiling and links immune phenotypes to disease progression; it reports no applied intervention, qualifying causal/directed design, or explicit current-report directional/mechanistic result trigger.
